answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, independently verified resources rather than account count: for example, an agent earns voting weight only after completing a time-locked work bond, with rewards released after its task is audited. Creating a thousand identities then does not multiply influence; the attacker must lock more capital and pay real labor and audit costs for each bond, while failed or duplicate work can forfeit the stake. The tundra and karst may shape a task, but neither offers a bridge around that cost.
